text: Every element of a coalgebra over a field lies in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra, the fundamental theorem recorded in [EGNO 1.20.4](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42). The source specializes its PID/free theorem: vector spaces are free, and finite generation becomes finite dimension. No multiplication, Hopf antipode or finite-dimensionality of the ambient coalgebra is assumed. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcoalgebra_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L169), [exists_finiteDimensional_subcoalgebra_of_setFinite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L237).
Checks the PID/free theorem specialized here.
Checks simultaneous containment of a finite set.

This family consists of subcoalgebras whose underlying R-modules are finitely generated. It is the finite-subcoalgebra family in the [fundamental theorem](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42), expressed for arbitrary commutative semirings. Finite refers to generators, not cardinality, and defining this family does not assert that it covers C; the covering theorem needs additional hypotheses. Checks pass: [mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L72), [sup_mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L85).
Checks the exact membership condition.
Checks closure under finite sums.

An explicit elementwise covering by finitely generated subcoalgebras implies that any finite subset lies in one such subcoalgebra. Taking a common finite join of its containing objects proves the claim. This is the finite-set consequence of the [fundamental theorem](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42), with coverage retained as a hypothesis over general semirings. Checks pass: [directedOn_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L94), [exists_finiteDimensional_subcoalgebra_of_setFinite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L237).
Checks common containing subcoalgebras exist.
Checks the field specialization with automatic coverage.

The family of finitely generated subcoalgebras is nonempty because it contains the zero subcoalgebra. Its underlying module has no required generators. This agrees with the [coalgebra axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41): a subcoalgebra has no multiplicative unit requirement. The result holds over commutative semirings and supplies the empty-finite-set case of subsequent containment arguments. Checks pass: [mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L72), [toRegularSubcomodule_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L103).
Checks that membership means module finiteness.
Checks the zero object is preserved by the regular-subcomodule interpretation.

Any two finitely generated subcoalgebras lie in a third: their sum, which is again finitely generated and stable under comultiplication. Thus the family is directed under inclusion, the structure behind the [fundamental theorem’s union description](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42). Directedness alone does not say that every element of an arbitrary semiring coalgebra is covered. Checks pass: [sup_mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L85), [mem_sSup_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L101).
Checks the explicit common upper bound stays finite.
Checks directed supremum membership reduces to one member.

Membership in the finite-subcoalgebra family is exactly finite generation of the underlying module; the equivalence unfolds its definition. This uses the finiteness convention of the [fundamental theorem over rings](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/10590/10590D.pdf#page=32). It does not mean that the carrier is a finite set, nor does it impose freeness on each member over an arbitrary semiring. Checks pass: [nonempty_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L79), [sup_mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L85).
Checks the zero-subcoalgebra case.
Checks the finite-generation condition survives binary joins.

A finite subset of a coalgebra over a field lies in a single finite-dimensional subcoalgebra. Apply the elementwise [fundamental theorem](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42), then take a finite sum of the resulting subcoalgebras. Here the subset is finite in cardinality, whereas the containing subcoalgebra is finite-dimensional and can have infinitely many elements. Checks pass: [exists_finiteDimensional_subcoalgebra_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L231), [exists_finite_subcoalgebra_of_setFinite_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L115).
Checks the elementwise field theorem.
Checks the finite-set passage from coverage.

The join of two finitely generated subcoalgebras is finitely generated. Its underlying module is their sum, so the union of two finite generating sets suffices; comultiplication remains in the sum’s tensor image. This is the finite-sum step behind the [fundamental theorem](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42), and requires no flatness or ambient finiteness. Checks pass: [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L75), [sup_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L176).
Checks the join is the module sum.
Checks finite generation of that sum.

For a coalgebra free over a principal ideal domain, every element lies in a finitely generated subcoalgebra, matching [Hazewinkel 8.4](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/10590/10590D.pdf#page=32). The source first finds a finite regular subcomodule; torsion-freeness makes it free over the PID, so its coefficient subcoalgebra works. Restricted counit evaluation recovers the original element. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L141), [matrixCoefficient_counit_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Regular.lean#L58).
Checks the finite regular-subcomodule input.
Checks the original element belongs to its coefficient subcoalgebra.

A subcoalgebra becomes a subcomodule of the regular right comodule on the same underlying submodule: Δ(D) in the image of D⊗D also lies in the image of D⊗C. This follows from the [coalgebra/comodule definitions](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The source uses tensor-map ranges, so it needs no assumption that these maps are injective. Checks pass: [toRegularSubcomodule_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L61), [mem_toRegularSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L68).
Checks the underlying submodule is unchanged.
Checks exactly the same elements are retained.

Forgetting the regular-subcomodule structure returns the original underlying submodule of D. The equality is definitional because the construction retains D’s carrier and weakens only the stability condition. This is the direct [coalgebra-to-comodule interpretation](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); no quotient, scalar extension or choice of coordinates changes the module. Checks pass: [mem_toRegularSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L68), [toRegularSubcomodule_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L162).
Checks equality of membership predicates.
Checks finite generation transfers through this unchanged module.

A subcoalgebra finitely generated as an R-module remains finitely generated when viewed as a regular subcomodule. The underlying submodule is identical, so the same generators work. This supports the finite-dimensional [coalgebra/comodule correspondence](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=42), while the native statement uses finite generation over a commutative semiring and requires no flatness. Checks pass: [toRegularSubcomodule_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L61), [mem_toRegularSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L68).
Checks the carrier module is unchanged.
Checks the corresponding membership identification.

For c in a subcoalgebra D, Δ(c) lies in the image of D⊗D→C⊗C. This exposes exactly the stored stability condition behind the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Over general semirings, tensor square here means that image; it does not assert injectivity of the tensor inclusion or automatically construct a coalgebra on the subtype. Checks pass: [comul_mem_tensorSquare_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L50), [comul_matrixCoefficient_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L135).
Checks stability of the entire ambient coalgebra.
Checks the explicit finite-basis coefficient formula used to construct coefficient subcoalgebras.

An element belongs to D viewed as a regular subcomodule exactly when it belongs to D as a subcoalgebra. This unfolds the shared carrier and agrees with the [regular-comodule interpretation](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The conversion only weakens two-factor comultiplication stability to right-comodule stability; it neither enlarges the set nor claims a converse correspondence. Checks pass: [toRegularSubcomodule_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L61), [toRegularSubcomodule_mono](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/RegularSubcomodule.lean#L75).
Checks equality of the whole underlying submodules.
Checks inclusion is preserved by the same identification.

Finitely generated subcomodules are closed under binary joins: the join has the sum of their underlying modules, generated by the two finite generating sets together. This is the finite-sum step in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). The source proves it over commutative semirings without assuming that C or M is free. Checks pass: [sup_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L200), [directedOn_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L201).
Checks finite generation of the join.
Checks the resulting directed-family property.

If every element belongs to some finitely generated subcomodule, their supremum is the entire comodule. Elementwise coverage proves the reverse inclusion into that supremum. This is the union conclusion underlying [Milne 4.7–8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), stated with an explicit covering hypothesis over semirings; the supremum itself need not be finitely generated. Checks pass: [mem_sSup_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L213), [iUnion_finiteSubcomodules_eq_univ_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L263).
Checks the exact membership interpretation.
Checks the corresponding literal-union conclusion.

Belonging to the supremum of finitely generated subcomodules means belonging to one member of that family. Finite sums can be absorbed into a common finite join because the family is nonempty and directed. This is the filtered-union mechanism in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), without claiming that the supremum already equals all of M. Checks pass: [directedOn_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L201), [coe_sSup_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L206).
Checks the directedness used.
Checks equality with the literal union of carriers.

The finitely generated subcomodules form a directed family under inclusion: the join of two is a finitely generated common upper bound. This matches the finite-sum argument beginning [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). Over the native commutative-semiring base, it requires neither finite generation of M nor a separate theorem that the family covers M. Checks pass: [supClosed_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L192), [mem_sSup_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L213).
Checks closure under the chosen upper bound.
Checks the resulting directed-union membership rule.

When C is free over R, every vector of a right C-comodule lies in a finitely generated subcomodule. Expand its coaction in a basis of C: coassociativity makes the finite coefficient span stable, and the counit recovers the vector. This extends [Milne 4.7’s proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97) to commutative semirings; M need not be free. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_setFinite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L272), [matrixCoefficient_counit_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Regular.lean#L58).
Checks the finite-set consequence of the same covering theorem.
Checks the regular-subcomodule counit calibration used by the coalgebra covering consumer.

The zero subcomodule belongs to the family of finitely generated subcomodules, so that family is nonempty even when M is zero. This supplies the empty-set boundary of the filtered-union construction in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). Finite means module generation, and this existence result does not require freeness of C. Checks pass: [mem_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L180), [coe_sSup_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L206).
Checks the membership condition used for zero.
Checks its role in the nonempty directed-union description.

This set collects the coaction-stable submodules of M that are finitely generated over R, the family used in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). The native definition works over commutative semirings and imposes no freeness. Finite generation becomes finite dimension over a field; it does not mean the submodule has finitely many elements. Checks pass: [mem_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L180), [supClosed_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L192).
Checks the definition’s exact condition.
Checks finite sums remain in the family.

Assuming every vector lies in a finitely generated subcomodule, any finite subset fits into a single such object. Directedness combines finitely many containing subcomodules; the zero object handles an empty subset. This is the finite-set form of [Milne 4.7’s filtered union](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), with coverage explicit over general commutative semirings. Checks pass: [directedOn_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L201), [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_fg_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L241).
Checks common upper bounds remain in the finite family.
Checks the stronger finite-span consequence.

An elementwise finite-subcomodule covering puts every finitely generated ordinary submodule P inside one finite subcomodule. Choose finitely many generators of P, contain them together, then use closure under linear combinations. This is the finite-span consequence of [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97); P need not itself be coaction-stable, and coverage remains an explicit hypothesis. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_setFinite_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L222), [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_fg](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L277).
Checks containment of the chosen finite generating set.
Checks specialization when a free coefficient coalgebra supplies coverage.

A finite subset of a comodule over a free coefficient coalgebra lies in one finitely generated subcomodule. The source combines its basis-derived elementwise covering with directed finite joins, extending [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97) to semirings. The freeness assumption is on C, not M; the empty subset is allowed. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L141), [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_setFinite_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L222).
Checks the elementwise free-coalgebra input.
Checks the finite-set passage from coverage.

The equivalence unfolds membership in the family of finite subcomodules: exactly the underlying R-module is finitely generated. This matches the finite-dimensional convention of [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97) over fields, while retaining the broader semiring statement. It adds no freeness, bounded dimension, finite carrier, or claim that these objects cover the ambient comodule. Checks pass: [nonempty_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L186), [supClosed_finiteSubcomodules](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L192).
Checks the zero object satisfies this condition.
Checks the condition is preserved by binary joins.

The extended real numbers consist of the ordinary reals together with two distinct endpoints, −∞ and +∞, ordered below and above every finite real. The definition adds exactly these two elements; they are not large finite numbers or overflow markers. Ordinary positive and negative reals remain distinct, and the two endpoints are separate from zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L35).

The map from ordinary reals to extended reals is the usual inclusion: it preserves the exact real value and its order, including negative values. Its image consists precisely of the finite extended reals, so it reaches neither infinity. This conversion performs no clipping, rounding, or replacement of exceptional values; it places a real inside the larger system. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L42).

The inclusion of nonnegative extended reals into extended reals preserves each finite nonnegative value and sends positive infinity to positive infinity. It does not pass through ordinary real conversion, which would lose infinity by replacing it with zero. The inclusion is injective and order preserving; its image is the nonnegative part of the extended real line. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L85).

Conversion from extended reals to ordinary reals preserves finite values but sends both −∞ and +∞ to zero. Those endpoint values are explicit defaults, not finite representations of infinity. Consequently this conversion is neither globally injective nor globally order preserving: although 1≤+∞, the converted values are 1 and 0, which reverse that comparison. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L228).

Conversion to nonnegative extended reals keeps nonnegative inputs, including +∞, and clips every negative input, including −∞, to zero. It is the extended positive-part operation. Unlike conversion to ordinary reals, it retains positive infinity. It also need not preserve addition: clipping −1 and 1 separately gives a sum of 1, while clipping their sum gives zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L712).

Extended-real multiplication agrees with ordinary multiplication on finite inputs and uses the usual sign rules when a factor is infinite. Lean explicitly sets zero times either infinity to zero; for example, (−∞)·(−2)=+∞ and (+∞)·(−∞)=−∞. This declaration installs that multiplication operation; additional algebraic laws are established separately rather than assumed by the operation itself. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L152).

For extended-real multiplication, 1 acts as an identity and 0 as an absorbing element on both sides, including at ±∞. Thus 1·(−∞)=−∞ and 0·(+∞)=0. These are precisely the laws packaged here. The structure does not assert associativity, distributivity, or cancellation; those stronger claims do not follow merely from having multiplication with zero and one. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L212).

The extended real line is a complete linear order: every subset has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound. In particular, the empty supremum is −∞ and the empty infimum is +∞. Adding the two endpoints supplies genuine bounds for empty or unbounded sets, unlike the zero defaults used for ordinary real suprema and infima. Compared with [Faris §5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L38).

Extended-real addition is associative and commutative, with zero as identity. Lean makes it defined everywhere by choosing (−∞)+(+∞)=−∞, with negative infinity absorbing every summand. Faris leaves that mixed-infinity expression undefined, so this is an explicit extension beyond classical partial arithmetic. The structure promises no additive inverses; infinity cannot be cancelled as though it were a real number. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L37).

Converting a finite extended real to an ordinary real and then including it back recovers the original value. Both exclusions, x≠+∞ and x≠−∞, are required for this identity. At either infinity the first conversion returns zero, so the round trip returns the finite value zero instead of the original endpoint. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L416).

If x≤y, x≠−∞, and y≠+∞, conversion to ordinary reals preserves that inequality. Together these assumptions force both values to be finite, even though only one infinity is excluded explicitly for each variable. The restrictions prevent failures such as 1≤+∞ converting to 1≤0, or −∞≤−1 converting to 0≤−1. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L410).

Clipping extended reals to their nonnegative part preserves weak order: x≤y implies toENNReal(x)≤toENNReal(y). No finiteness or sign assumptions are required, because −∞ maps to zero and +∞ remains +∞. Strict order need not survive; for example, −2<−1 but both values are clipped to zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L783).

Including a nonnegative extended real in the full extended real line and then converting back recovers the original value, including +∞. The first map introduces no negative values, so clipping loses nothing. The explicit infinity case matters: a detour through ordinary real conversion would send +∞ to zero and would not satisfy this round-trip identity. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L765).

For an ordinary real x, including it in the extended reals and then converting to nonnegative extended reals gives its positive part, max(x,0). Thus negative inputs become zero and nonnegative inputs retain their value. No infinity can appear from this finite input; the first inclusion is exact, while the second conversion performs the clipping. Compared with [Faris §8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L771).

Every extended real other than +∞ is at most the value obtained by converting it to an ordinary real and including it back. For finite inputs this is equality. The remaining allowed case is −∞, which becomes zero and therefore increases. Excluding +∞ is essential, since its conversion also gives zero but would decrease the value. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L420).

Including the sum of two ordinary real numbers in the extended reals gives the same result as adding their inclusions. Both inputs are finite, may have either sign, and retain ordinary real arithmetic. The statement therefore does not involve the chosen value of (+∞)+(−∞); neither endpoint can occur from either input or their real sum. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L310).

Including a real product in the extended reals agrees with multiplying the two included real factors. The factors may be positive, negative, or zero; no sign restrictions are needed because both remain finite. This is preservation of ordinary real multiplication, and does not rely on or assert any cancellation law for infinite extended-real factors. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L155).

Two extended reals satisfy a<b exactly when some finite ordinary real lies strictly between them. The endpoints may themselves be infinite: one can choose a real above any finite lower endpoint, below any finite upper endpoint, or zero between the two infinities. For two finite endpoints, ordinary real density supplies the intermediate value. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L863).

Every nonnegative extended real remains nonnegative when included in the full extended real line. This includes +∞, so the conclusion is not a finiteness claim. The source type already excludes negative values and −∞; the inclusion preserves its order and zero, which explains why no separate hypothesis on the input is needed. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L660).

Converting a real x to nonnegative extended reals and then including it in the full extended real line produces the finite value max(x,0). The first conversion clips negative inputs; the later inclusion cannot recover them. For example, −1 becomes zero, whereas 1 stays 1. This distinguishes the composite map from the direct real inclusion. Compared with [Faris §8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/EReal/Basic.lean#L592).

Every positive definite unimodular integral lattice of rank n≤9 is isometric to ℤⁿ with its standard dot product, E₈, or ℤ⊕E₈ with orthogonal summands. Isometry preserves the form and maps the entire lattice onto the target. Rank preservation restricts the exceptional cases to ranks eight and nine; the zero lattice is included. See [Chenevier, Unimodular hunting, §1.1 and Table1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.18788v1). Checks pass: [rank-eight uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/PosDef/SmallRankUnimodular.lean#L431), [small-rank minimum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/PosDef/SmallRankUnimodular.lean#L129), [E8 parity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/Basic.lean#L753), [unimodularity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/Basic.lean#L782), [minimum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/Basic.lean#L758).
Even unimodular positive rank-eight specialization is E8
A nonzero positive unimodular lattice of rank at most five has minimum one
The actual E8 Cartan lattice is even
The actual E8 Cartan determinant gives unimodularity
The E8 model has minimum two

Two unimodular integral lattices are isometric over ℝ and over every ℤₚ exactly when their positive and negative indices agree and their parity agrees. Even means every vector has even squared length. The encoded signature also records nullity, automatically zero here; equality of signature means more than equality of the difference of its indices. See [Nikulin, Theorem0.2.1(a), p.104](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=rus&paperid=1677&what=fullteng). Checks pass: [parity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/Genus.lean#L134), [dyadic criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/Dyadic/Unimodular.lean#L131), [same-genus family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/EvenUnimodularGenus.lean#L70), [non-isometry](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/EvenUnimodularGenus.lean#L79).

Every form-preserving automorphism of the E₈ lattice is a finite product of root reflections x↦x−B(r,x)r, where B(r,r)=2. Thus the generated subgroup is the full lattice isometry group. Here norm means squared length, and subgroup closure means algebraic generation. Reflections have determinant −1, so orientation-reversing isometries are included. See [Romano–Thorne, §2, p.682](https://api.repository.cam.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/3268ec23-164a-432c-a456-75ec7559478f/content). Checks pass: [reflection compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/WeylGroup.lean#L239), [240 roots](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/Roots.lean#L109), [negation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/WeylGroup.lean#L271), [group order](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeE/WeylGroup.lean#L287), [determinant](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Isometry/Reflection.lean#L93).
